title: Breathing and quadrupole modes in squeezed Bose-Bose liquid drops
authors: Marko Korda, Leandra Vranješ Markić, Jordi Boronat
abstract: We investigate the lowest excitation modes of binary $^{39}$K ultradilute droplets confined harmonically in one direction, which reduces the critical number of particles needed to sustain a self-bound state. Using the density functional built from first-principles quantum Monte Carlo calculations (QMC), which incorporates the effects of finite range interactions, we study the crossover of the oscillation modes from three to two dimensions. For weak squeezing, we observe the coupling between breathing and quadrupole modes, resulting from the breaking of spherical symmetry. Increasing the squeezing, the higher-frequency mode corresponding to three-dimensional breathing mode becomes unstable. For squeezings stronger and comparable to experiments, we analyze the dependence of the excitation modes on the droplet size for several interactions and show the reduction of the number of particles needed to sustain stable oscillations. The differences between the results obtained with the QMC functional and the extended Gross-Pitaevskii theory are increased with respect to the case of previously studied spherical droplets.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates the collective oscillation modes (breathing and quadrupole) in squeezed Bose-Bose liquid droplets using advanced Quantum Monte Carlo density functionals. Key findings demonstrate how external squeezing modifies mode coupling and reduces the minimum particle count required for stable oscillations. It is crucial for understanding the dynamics of quantum matter under anisotropic confinement.
main_problem: The study investigates the lowest excitation modes (breathing and quadrupole) of squeezed Bose-Bose liquid drops and how these modes change with external confinement and interaction strength.
main_result: The research shows that squeezing causes mode coupling and instability in the breathing mode, while the critical number of particles needed for stable oscillations is reduced compared to unsqueezed cases.
method: The authors use Density Functional Theory (DFT) built from first-principles Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) calculations to analyze the time evolution of density moments.
model_or_system: The system is a binary ultradilute Bose-Bose liquid drop (e.g., $^{39}	ext{K}$) confined harmonically in one direction, allowing for the study of crossover from 3D to 2D behavior.
key_observables: Monopole moment ($\langle Q_0(t) angle$) and quadrupole moment ($\langle Q_2(t) angle$) oscillation frequencies, anisotropy ratios ($\kappa_s, \kappa_a$), and the critical particle number for stable oscillations.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($f$), droplet size ($N$), interaction strengths ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma$), and the external harmonic confinement potential.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linear response theory for small perturbations, and comparisons are made between QMC functionals and Mean-Field + LHY approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the frequency intensity distribution vs. squeezing parameter, time evolution of moments for different squeezing strengths, and mode frequencies versus atom number for various confinement regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the theoretical framework using QMC-derived functionals, analyzing the mode coupling and instability as squeezing increases, and finally comparing the results across different confinement regimes and theoretical approximations.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed insights into collective excitations in highly controllable quantum systems like ultracold atomic droplets, bridging the gap between mean-field descriptions and full quantum many-body treatments.
